title: Mitochondrial Structure and Function
learning_goals: Identify the main structural components of a mitochondrion
Explain how the structure supports energy production
Describe the role of mitochondrial DNA

segments.text: Let's start with the outer boundary of the organelle. This membrane separates the mitochondrion from the rest of the cell.
Just inside, we have the intermembrane space, a thin compartment that holds important ions for the next steps.
The inner membrane is highly folded, creating many cristae that dramatically increase surface area.
These folds, the cristae, host the protein complexes that carry out oxidative phosphorylation.
Inside the inner membrane lies the matrix, a gel-like space that contains enzymes for the citric acid cycle.
Embedded in the matrix is the mitochondrial DNA, which encodes some of the proteins needed for respiration.
The inner membrane hosts the electron transport chain, where electrons are passed along a series of carriers.
The flow of electrons creates a proton gradient that powers ATP synthase to make the cell's main energy currency.
In summary, the layered structure—from outer membrane to cristae—organizes the biochemical steps that turn nutrients into ATP.
